questions.question: The Lokpal of India celebrated its 1st Foundation Day on which date in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jan 16 2026 **__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Lokpal of India** celebrated its **1st Foundation Day** on **16 January 2026**. This is an important milestone for the institution, marking its establishment and operationalization.
 
• The Lokpal was constituted under the **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013**, aimed at addressing corruption and enhancing transparency in governance.
 
• The institution of Lokpal is responsible for investigating complaints of corruption against public servants, including the **Prime Minister (with certain exceptions)**, ministers, and other public officials.
 
• The **Foundation Day celebrations** signify the commencement of the Lokpal’s role in promoting accountability and integrity within governmental processes.
 
• The **Chairperson** and other members of the Lokpal are appointed by a selection committee comprising the **Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India, Speaker of Lok Sabha, and an eminent jurist**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013:**

 
 
• The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act was enacted in **2013** to address corruption and ensure accountability in public offices.
 
• The Act mandates the establishment of a **Lokpal** at the central level and **Lokayuktas** at the state level.
 
• The Lokpal is empowered to investigate complaints against **public servants**, including ministers, parliamentarians, and bureaucrats, but excludes complaints against the judiciary.
 
 
 
• **Composition of Lokpal:**
 
 
• The Lokpal consists of a **Chairperson** and up to **eight members**, with 50% of the members from judicial backgrounds and at least 50% from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, minorities, and women.
 
• The Chairperson must be a former Chief Justice of India, a Supreme Court judge, or an eminent person with expertise in anti-corruption policies.
 
 
 
• **Selection Process:**
 
 
• The Chairperson and members are selected by a committee comprising the **Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India, Speaker of Lok Sabha, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, and an eminent jurist**.
 
• The selection process ensures transparency and fairness in appointing individuals to these critical roles.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Lokpal:**
 
 
• The Lokpal has the power to **prosecute public servants**, confiscate ill-gotten wealth, and impose penalties.
 
• It functions autonomously and is not subject to the directions of any government authority.
 
• It has jurisdiction over central government officials, including complaints against the **Prime Minister**, with certain restrictions.
 
 
 
• **Important Developments:**
 
 
• The Lokpal began functioning in **March 2019**, following the appointment of its Chairperson, **Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose**.
 
• The institution is seen as a pivotal step in strengthening India’s anti-corruption framework.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Provisions:**

 
 
• The Lokpal has the power to order investigations through agencies like the **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)**.
 
• It can also recommend disciplinary action against public servants found guilty of corruption.
 
• All public servants are required to disclose their assets and liabilities to the Lokpal.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• The Lokpal faces challenges related to staffing, infrastructure, and procedural delays.
 
• Ensuring independence and avoiding political interference are critical for its effective functioning.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• The establishment of Lokpal is a significant step towards curbing corruption and promoting good governance.
 
• It fosters public trust in the government by ensuring accountability and transparency in administration.

questions.question: As per revised Reserve Bank of India guidelines in April 2025, from what minimum age can minors independently open and operate savings accounts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Revised RBI Guidelines (April 2025):** The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** issued updated guidelines allowing minors aged **10 years** or older to independently open and operate savings accounts without requiring a guardian or parent.
 
• **Empowering Financial Independence:** This move aims to promote **financial literacy** and **independence** among young individuals, encouraging them to understand and manage their finances from an early age.
 
• **Eligibility Criteria:** Minors must meet the age threshold of **10 years** and comply with bank-specific requirements, such as providing necessary documentation like birth certificates or school IDs.
 
• **Account Features:** Banks typically impose certain limitations on minor-operated accounts, such as **transaction caps** and restrictions on overdrafts, to ensure safe usage while teaching financial responsibility.
 
• **Bank-Specific Policies:** While RBI sets the baseline guidelines, individual banks may implement additional features or rules for minor accounts, such as linking them to guardian accounts or offering tailored benefits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Purpose of RBI Guidelines:**

 
 
• To promote **financial inclusion** by enabling younger individuals to access banking services.
 
• To instill **discipline** and knowledge about savings, spending, and banking processes early in life.
 
 
 
• **Global Practices:**
 
 
• Many countries, such as **United States** and **United Kingdom**, offer similar provisions for minors to open savings accounts, emphasizing global trends in fostering financial independence.
 
• The age limit varies by country, with some allowing accounts to be opened by minors younger than **10 years**, but with stricter parental oversight.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Minor Savings Accounts:**
 
 
• Encourages **financial planning** and budgeting skills at an early age.
 
• Provides minors with a secure place to save allowances, gifts, or earnings.
 
• Helps in building a foundation for future financial activities, such as opening full-fledged accounts or availing loans.
 
 
 
• **Important RBI Guidelines:**
 
 
• Minors can access savings accounts independently if they are at least **10 years old**.
 
• Such accounts can be operated for **basic banking services**, including deposits, withdrawals, and online transactions under limited thresholds.
 
• Guardians may still retain oversight in certain cases, depending on the bank’s internal policies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Framework:** Banks are required to adhere to RBI guidelines while ensuring compliance with **Know Your Customer (KYC)** norms for minor accounts.
 
• **Parental Controls:** Banks may offer additional features like **parental notifications** or transaction monitoring for minors operating accounts independently.
 
• **Educational Outreach:** Financial institutions and schools often collaborate to educate minors about **financial literacy**, leveraging these accounts as practical learning tools.
 
• **Digital Banking:** With the rise of **digital banking**, minors can also access mobile banking apps or online portals under controlled settings.

questions.question: Which award did former cyclist Sucha Singh receive in 2025?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Arjuna Award** is one of India's prestigious sports honors, instituted in **1961**, to recognize exceptional achievements in sports and athletics.
 
• It includes a **bronze statue of Arjuna**, a **certificate**, and a **cash prize**. As of recent updates, the cash prize associated with the award is **₹15 lakh**.
 
• The Lifetime category of the Arjuna Award is specifically intended to honor **athletes who have displayed exemplary dedication and achievements over their entire career**, serving as role models for younger generations.
 
• **Sucha Singh**, a former cyclist, received the Arjuna Award under the Lifetime Achievement category in **2025** for his outstanding contribution to Indian cycling and his role in promoting the sport at various levels.
 
• The award recognizes not only the recipient’s sporting achievements but also their efforts in mentoring and uplifting the sport in their region or nation. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Arjuna Award:**

 
 
• The Arjuna Award was established by the Government of India to recognize **exceptional achievements in sports** and to motivate athletes to continue excelling in their respective fields.
 
• Recipients are chosen based on their **performance over the last four years**, consistent excellence, and their contribution to the promotion of sports.
 
• It covers a wide range of sports disciplines, including mainstream sports, indigenous sports, and para-sports.
 
• Famous past recipients include **Sachin Tendulkar, P.V. Sindhu, and Abhinav Bindra**.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility for Lifetime Arjuna Award:**
 
 
• The Lifetime Achievement category is awarded to sportspersons who have **dedicated their lives to sports**, achieving excellence and contributing significantly to the development of their sport.
 
• It is not limited to recent performances but also considers the recipient's **long-term contributions** to the field.
 
• The selection process involves recommendations from a committee appointed by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
 
 
 
• **Sucha Singh’s Contribution:**
 
 
• **Sucha Singh** is a renowned cyclist who represented India in various national and international competitions.
 
• He played a pivotal role in **popularizing cycling** across different regions, especially in rural parts of the country.
 
• His lifetime dedication to cycling and mentoring young athletes was recognized with the Lifetime Achievement Arjuna Award.
 
 
 
• **Other Sports Awards in India:**
 
 
• **Khel Ratna Award:** The highest sporting honor in India, awarded for outstanding performance at the international level over a period of four years.
 
• **Dronacharya Award:** Given to coaches for their exemplary role in training athletes to achieve excellence in sports.
 
• **MAKA Trophy:** Presented to the best university for sports in India, recognizing the role of educational institutions in promoting sports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of Arjuna Award:**

 
 
• It aims to **encourage athletes** to achieve higher levels of performance and represent India internationally.
 
• The selection process is rigorous, ensuring that only deserving candidates are honored based on **merit** and contribution.
 
• Awardees serve as **ambassadors of Indian sports**, inspiring young athletes to strive for excellence.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Arjuna Award has been instrumental in **highlighting the significance of sports** as a profession in India.
 
• It has contributed to the **development of sports culture** and recognition of athletes from various socioeconomic backgrounds.

questions.question: Who took over as the Chairperson of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tuhin Kanta Pandey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tuhin Kanta Pandey** was appointed as the **Chairperson of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** in **March 2025**. This is a pivotal role that oversees the regulation of the securities market in India.
 
• He succeeded **Madhabi Puri Buch**, who was the first woman to lead SEBI, marking another significant leadership transition for the regulatory body.
 
• **Tuhin Kanta Pandey** was previously the **Secretary of the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM)** under the Ministry of Finance, where he played a crucial role in managing India's disinvestment program.
 
• The selection of the SEBI Chairperson is a highly scrutinized process, typically undertaken by a high-level committee consisting of senior government officials and experts, ensuring the appointee has the necessary expertise and experience in financial markets and governance.
 
• The tenure of the SEBI Chairperson is typically **three years**, extendable based on performance and the government's discretion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India):**

 
 
• SEBI was established in **1988** and given statutory powers on **30th January 1992**, through the SEBI Act, 1992.
 
• It is headquartered in **Mumbai, Maharashtra**, with regional offices in key cities like Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, and Ahmedabad.
 
• The primary functions of SEBI include protecting the interests of investors, regulating the securities market, and promoting its development.
 
• SEBI also monitors and regulates the activities of stock exchanges, brokers, sub-brokers, and other intermediaries.
 
 
 
• **Tuhin Kanta Pandey's Contributions:**
 
 
• As the Secretary of DIPAM, he spearheaded several successful disinvestment programs, including the strategic sale of **Air India** in 2021, a landmark achievement in India's economic reforms.
 
• He has extensive experience in financial management, public policy, and governance, making him a strong candidate for the SEBI Chairperson role.
 
• His expertise in asset monetization and public finance aligns with SEBI's goals of ensuring market efficiency and investor protection.
 
 
 
• **Key Challenges for SEBI Chairperson:**
 
 
• Ensuring market stability amidst global economic uncertainties and fostering investor confidence.
 
• Strengthening regulations to curb insider trading, market manipulation, and other fraudulent activities.
 
• Promoting financial literacy and inclusion among retail investors.
 
• Leveraging technology and innovation to enhance market transparency and efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Madhabi Puri Buch:** She served as SEBI Chairperson from **March 2022** to **March 2025** and was the first woman to hold this position.
 
• **Shaktikanta Das:** He is the **Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** since **December 2018**, with no involvement in SEBI leadership.
 
• **Arvind Panagariya:** An economist and former Vice Chairman of **NITI Aayog**, he has no direct association with SEBI.
 
• **Option 5:** This option is invalid and does not pertain to the question.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **SEBI's Key Functions:**

 
 
• Regulating the stock exchanges and securities market in India.
 
• Monitoring and regulating mutual funds, venture capital, and alternative investment funds.
 
• Ensuring the fair and transparent functioning of the securities market.
 
• Educating investors and enhancing their understanding of financial markets.
 
 
 
• **Significance of SEBI:**
 
 
• SEBI plays a critical role in maintaining the integrity and efficiency of Indian financial markets.
 
• It ensures that companies adhere to regulatory norms and safeguards the interests of small and retail investors.
 
• By promoting corporate governance, SEBI fosters transparency and accountability in the financial ecosystem.

• The event took place on **January 1, 2025**, marking the official launch of this initiative to enhance India's capabilities in genomic data analysis and research.

• **GenomeIndia Project**:

 
 
• The **GenomeIndia Project** is a national initiative launched by the Government of India to map the genetic diversity of the Indian population.
 
• It aims to collect and analyze genome samples from across the country to build a comprehensive database for scientific research and healthcare applications.
 
• This project is expected to help identify genetic disorders, improve disease diagnosis, and facilitate the development of personalized medicine.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Genomics**:

• Advancements in genomics have paved the way for revolutionary technologies like CRISPR and personalized gene therapy.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Genomic Data**:
 
 
• Genomic data is used in **healthcare** for early diagnosis of diseases, drug development, and creating personalized treatment plans.
 
• In agriculture, it helps in **crop improvement** and developing pest-resistant varieties.
 
• It also has applications in **forensic science** for solving crimes and identifying individuals.
 
 
 
• **Global Genomic Initiatives**:

questions.question: Which of the following Indian Constitutional Amendment Acts is also known as Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**106th Constitutional Amendment Bill**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **106th Constitutional Amendment Bill** is popularly referred to as the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam**, which translates to "Women Empowerment Act" in English.
 
• It aims to provide **33% reservation for women** in the **Lok Sabha** (House of the People) and the **State Legislative Assemblies**.
 
• This bill was introduced with the objective of **enhancing the political participation of women** in India, ensuring gender equity in decision-making processes.
 
• The constitutional amendment ensures that the seats reserved for women will rotate periodically among different constituencies, ensuring **fair representation** across all regions.
 
• It highlights India's commitment to achieving **gender equality** as outlined in the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG-5)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The demand for **women’s reservation** in legislative bodies has been a long-standing issue in India, with various political parties and activists advocating for it since the 1990s.
 
• The **84th Amendment Bill** in 1999 and the **Women’s Reservation Bill** introduced in 2008 were earlier attempts that faced hurdles in Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Global Practices:**
 
 
• Countries like **Rwanda**, **Sweden**, and **Norway** have implemented similar measures, with Rwanda having the highest percentage of women in Parliament globally at over **60%**.
 
• India ranks **148th** globally in terms of women’s representation in Parliament, underscoring the need for such reforms.
 
 
 
• **Implementation:**
 
 
• The **106th Constitutional Amendment** requires the approval of both Houses of Parliament with a two-thirds majority and ratification by at least **50% of state legislatures**.
 
• Once enacted, this reservation will initially apply for a period of **15 years**, after which it may be extended based on necessity.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• This amendment is expected to **bridge the gender gap** in political representation, fostering inclusive governance.
 
• It will provide a platform for women to address issues like **healthcare, education, and gender-based violence** more effectively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**

 
 
• Article **81** deals with the composition of the Lok Sabha, and this amendment introduces specific provisions for women’s reservation.
 
• Article **170** covers the composition of State Legislative Assemblies, where similar reservations will be applied.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• Ensuring the effective implementation of this reservation without political or social resistance may be challenging.
 
• Critics have raised concerns about the potential **tokenism** of women in politics if not accompanied by broader systemic reforms.
 
 
 
• **Way Forward:**
 
 
• Capacity-building programs and leadership training for women are essential to make this reservation impactful.
 
• Efforts to promote gender equality in political parties and grassroots governance structures should complement this amendment.

questions.question: Approximately how many hectares are targeted for increased forest and tree cover by 2030 as per the Revised Green India Mission (GIM) Plan released in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**24.7 million hectares**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Revised Green India Mission (GIM) Plan**, released in **2025**, aims to increase forest and tree cover by approximately **24.7 million hectares** by the year **2030**.
 
• The Green India Mission is one of the **eight missions** under the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), launched by the **Government of India** to address climate change challenges.
 
• The mission focuses on **ecosystem restoration**, **afforestation**, and **reforestation** in degraded forest lands and other areas, contributing to improved **carbon sequestration** and enhanced biodiversity.
 
• Under the revised plan, the mission has set ambitious targets to **restore degraded ecosystems**, improve the quality of forest cover, and enhance ecosystem services such as **water security**, **soil fertility**, and **livelihood generation**.
 
• It is part of India's commitment to achieving its **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** under the **Paris Agreement** to combat climate change through sustainable forest management and increased green cover.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green India Mission (GIM):**

 
 
• GIM was launched in **2010** as part of the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)**.
 
• Its primary objective is to increase the forest cover and improve ecosystem services such as **biodiversity conservation**, **water catchment protection**, and **carbon sequestration**.
 
• The mission emphasizes **community participation** in forest management and conservation efforts.
 
• It also focuses on enhancing the **livelihood opportunities** of forest-dependent communities through sustainable practices.
 
 
 
• **Paris Agreement and India's NDCs:**
 
 
• India's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement aim to achieve a reduction in the **emissions intensity** of its GDP by **33-35%** by **2030**, compared to **2005** levels.
 
• The Green India Mission contributes to India's **land use and forestry** commitments by enhancing carbon sinks.
 
• India has pledged to create an additional **carbon sink of 2.5 to 3 billion tonnes** of CO₂ equivalent through increased forest and tree cover.
 
 
 
• **Global Context of Afforestation:**
 
 
• Afforestation and reforestation initiatives are critical components of global efforts to address **climate change** and achieve **sustainable development goals**.
 
• Organizations such as the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)** highlight the role of forests in **carbon sequestration** and mitigating climate change impacts.
 
• Countries worldwide are implementing similar programs to restore degraded lands and increase forest cover, aligning with international goals like the **Bonn Challenge** and **REDD+**.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• India's forests serve as a critical resource for **carbon sequestration**, helping to mitigate the effects of **global warming**.
 
• Afforestation programs contribute to improving **soil fertility**, preventing **soil erosion**, and ensuring **water security** in forest-dependent regions.
 
• The Green India Mission promotes the adoption of **climate-resilient practices** in agricultural and forestry sectors, enhancing the sustainability of ecosystems.
 
• Increased green cover helps in conserving **native flora** and **fauna**, safeguarding India's rich biodiversity.
